questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding infective endocarditis except:

options.label: A
options.text: Subacute IE is caused by organisms with lower virulence (e.g., viridans streptococci)

options.label: B
options.text: Acute endocarditis is a necrotizing and ulcerative, invasive valvular infection on a previously normal valve

options.label: C
options.text: S. viridans is the major offender in IE among intravenous drug abusers

options.label: D
options.text: Prosthetic valve endocarditis can be caused by S epidermidis

questions.answerText: S. viridans is the major offender in IE among intravenous drug abusers
questions.solutionHtml:
S. viridans is the major offender in IE among intravenous drug abusers
  • False, aureus is the major offender in IE among intravenous drug abusers.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 563

questions.stem: The following statement is true regarding vegetations of infective endocarditis except:

options.label: B
options.text: Aortic and mitral valves are most commonly affected

options.label: D
options.text: Doesn’t involve more than one valve

questions.answerText: Doesn’t involve more than one valve
questions.solutionHtml:
Doesn’t involve more than one valve
  • False, vegetations can be single or multiple and may involve more than one valve


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 563, 564

questions.stem: Dukes criteria are used for the diagnosis of-
questions.solutionHtml:
Infective endocarditis
  • The so-called modified Duke criteria facilitate the evaluation of individuals with suspected Infective Endocarditis (IE) that takes into account predisposing factors, physical findings, and blood culture results.
  • MNEMONIC: Duke’s criteria are used for Infective Endocarditis (DIE).


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 563, 564

options.text: Roth spot- Hemorrhagic spot on palm and sole

options.label: C
options.text: Osler nodes- painful subcutaneous nodules on finger and toe

options.label: D

questions.answerText: Roth spot- Hemorrhagic spot on palm and sole
questions.solutionHtml:
Roth spot- Hemorrhagic spot on palm and sole

Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 564
